description:
# India crime data you can trace

Official crime statistics from India's **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**, cleaned into one tidy table and linked to the exact document each number came from, plus classified crime-news metadata. Rebuilt automatically every day.

## Start here
| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `crime_state_year.csv` | **The clean table.** One row per state/UT x year x crime head x measure (cases registered, persons arrested, convicted, victims ...). Only numbers whose state rows add up to NCRB's own all-India figure; duplicates across files collapsed; disagreements flagged in `disputed`. |
| `crime_india_year.csv` | The same for **all of India**: NCRB's national crime-head tables plus the all-India row of every state table, so 2001-2015 and 2018 onward join up. |
| `documents.csv` | Every source document: title, publisher, original URL, Internet Archive permalink, and how many numbers it gave. Join on `file`. |
| `facts.parquet` | Everything NCRB's Excel tables contain, one number per row (states, districts, cities, crime heads), with metric, category, year, `qc` flag and full provenance. About 7 million rows. |
| `news.parquet`, `news_events.parquet` | Crime stories from Indian news feeds: category, state, district, victim group, stage of the case, link, one-line summary; and one row per distinct event. |
| `facts_pdf_lowconf.parquet` | The same, extracted from archived PDFs. Check against the source before use. |
| `ref_states.csv`, `ref_categories.csv` | Code lists. |
| `PROFILE.md`, `DATA_DICTIONARY.md` | Coverage and known gaps (regenerated every run); every column explained. |

The other files (`facts_raw.parquet`, `parse_state.json`, `unmapped_states.csv`, `news_snapshots.txt`, `news_rejected.txt`) are the pipeline's working state; ignore them.
The original PDFs and spreadsheets are in the companion dataset **crimebase-raw**: a row's `file` is `raw-<first character of file>/<file>` there.

## Quick start
```python
import glob, pandas as pd
D = glob.glob('/kaggle/input/**/crime_state_year.csv', recursive=True)[0].rsplit('/', 1)[0]   # the dataset's folder, wherever Kaggle mounts it
p = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/crime_state_year.csv')

# murders registered in India under the IPC, by year
n = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/crime_india_year.csv')
m = n[(n.scope == 'ipc') & (n.crime_head == 'Murder') & (n.metric == 'cases_registered')]
print(m.set_index('year').value)

# where did a number come from?
docs = pd.read_csv(f'{D}/documents.csv')
print(m.merge(docs[['file', 'source_url', 'wayback_url']], on='file').iloc[0])

# state by state, 2015
st = p[(p.scope == 'ipc') & (p.crime_head == 'Murder') & (p.metric == 'cases_registered') & (p.year == 2015)]
print(st.nlargest(5, 'value')[['state', 'value']])

# crime news: distinct events by category
e = pd.read_parquet(f'{D}/news_events.parquet')
print(e.groupby('category').size().sort_values())
```
A worked example is in the notebook **CrimeBase quickstart**.

## Why you can rely on it
* **Sourced**: every row names its document; documents carry the original URL and the Internet Archive permalink of the exact capture.
* **Checked**: state values are summed and compared with NCRB's own all-India row (`qc` in `facts.parquet`; only `sum_ok` rows enter the state table).
* **Honest**: conflicting values are kept and flagged, years are never guessed from ranges, and inferred fields (metric, category) are labelled as inferred.
* **No redundancy**: identical files are stored once; identical facts collapse to one row.
* **Private by design**: no FIR or victim-level data; headlines and summaries of sexual-offence and child-victim stories are withheld.

## Know the limits
Reported crime is not actual crime: registration practices differ by state and year, and the move from IPC to BNS (2024 onward) needs care across years. Coverage follows what NCRB published as spreadsheets; some years are PDF-only (see `PROFILE.md` for the exact map). News is a sample of public feeds, not a census. `scope` matters: the same head (rape, murder) appears in several table families that overlap, so never add across scopes.

## Updates and credit
Refreshed daily by an open-source pipeline (AGPL-3.0): https://github.com/chandranshB/CrimeBase. Maintained by Chandransh. If this helps your work, a citation is appreciated: *Chandransh, CrimeBase: source-cited India crime data (Kaggle / GitHub, chandranshB/CrimeBase).* Corrections are welcome on GitHub. Government data is published under India's open data policy. Place names are resolved to states with GeoNames data (CC BY 4.0), so city and district rows and news headlines carry a state even when none is printed; such rows are marked (state_inferred, state_basis).
